definitions.definition: A household or commercial appliance used for keeping food fresh by refrigeration (short form fridge).

quote.citation: 1868, Louisa May Alcott, Little Women, ch. 11:
quote.text: Jo uttered a groan and fell back in her chair, remembering that she had given a last hasty powdering to the berries out of one of the two boxes on the kitchen table, and had neglected to put the milk in the refrigerator.

quote.citation: 2013 June 1, “A better waterworks”, in The Economist‎[1], volume 407, number 8838, page 5 (Technology Quarterly):
quote.text: An artificial kidney these days still means a refrigerator-sized dialysis machine. Such devices mimic the way real kidneys cleanse blood and eject impurities and surplus water as urine.

definitions.definition: A similar device used to keep non-food items cold, such as blood, photographic film, drugs, or pharmaceuticals like insulin.
One who has a chilling influence.

quote.citation: 1852 March – 1853 September, Charles Dickens, Bleak House, London: Bradbury and Evans, […], published 1853, →OCLC:
quote.text: […]  in a state of sublime satisfaction, he moves among the company, a magnificent refrigerator.
